For a window of 5 values and degree 2, the weights from the code are:

\[
c = \begin{bmatrix}
  -0.08571 & 0.34286 & 0.48571 & 0.34286 & -0.08571
\end{bmatrix} = \frac{1}{35}\begin{bmatrix}
  -3 & 12 & 17 & 12 & -3
\end{bmatrix}
\]

These are the classic weights from the 1964 paper. They add up to 1, and the two outer weights are negative. The negative weights let the fit follow a peak instead of flattening it. For the row 40, 60, 200, 60, 40 the filter gives (-3 x 40 + 12 x 60 + 17 x 200 + 12 x 60 - 3 x 40) / 35 = 131.43. A box filter of the same size gives 80.
